_doc.purpose: The award universe the site is built on, and how a venue's prestige is computed from it. Every number here is data, not code: change a weight, re-run src/build_venues.py, and the roster re-scores. Nothing in src/ hard-codes an honor or a point value.
_doc.why_a_config: The same reason config/rubric.json exists. A composite score that cannot be argued with is a score nobody should trust, so the inputs are published next to the output and a reader can disagree with the weights without reading Python.
_doc.missing_data_rule: A venue's prestige uses ONLY the honors it actually holds. There is no imputation here, unlike rubric.json: an award is a fact or it is absent, and absence is not an average.
_doc.recency_rule: Points decay with the age of the venue's MOST RECENT honor, never with the age of the individual award. A 1995 James Beard winner that took a 2025 Michelin star is scored as a current restaurant, which it is.

michelin.label: Michelin
michelin.note: 2025 NYC selection. Every record carries a street address, so these merge on name AND address and are the safest rows in the set.

james_beard.label: James Beard
james_beard.note: 1991-2026, NYC only. The award is often to a CHEF, so `name` is a person and `restaurant` is the venue. No addresses at all, which is why these merge on a unique name or not at all.

nyt.label: New York Times
nyt.note: The 2026 Top 100 plus one starred review. Only 5 of 101 carry an address; the rank is recoverable from the notes field and is worth keeping, because No. 1 and No. 97 are not the same honor.

honors._doc: points = the venue's base score if this is its best honor. Ordered highest first within each source; `rank` orders the badge display.

nyt_rank_bonus._doc: The Top 100 is a ranked list and the rank is public, so use it. A linear ramp: No. 1 earns the full bonus, No. 100 earns none.

breadth_bonus._doc: Agreement between independent juries is evidence. Michelin, the Beard Foundation and the Times reaching the same restaurant separately says more than any one of them saying it twice.

recency._doc: Multiplier applied to the total, keyed on years since the venue's most recent honor. A restaurant last recognised in 1998 is a piece of history, not a booking recommendation, and the roster should say so without hiding it.

closed_penalty._doc: A closed restaurant keeps its honors -- they were earned -- but must never outrank somewhere you can actually book. The multiplier is applied last and is deliberately blunt.
